text:
rav: Quick sync — we need to finalize what goes into Phase 1 of the routing/segmentation initiative. Customers keep pushing for guarantees, but infra has concerns about cost and complexity.

leah: Key ask from CS: per-tenant affinity that respects data residency. They want a toggle in the console not a ticket.

rav: Console toggle implies APIs + audit trail. Ops: can we support that without a heavy rollout burden?

tom: We can, but need to decide the enforcement model: soft affinity (best-effort) vs hard pin (always route). Hard pin increases capacity footprint.

jordana: Sales: some named accounts will pay for hard pin. We should model incremental cost and productize as a paid add-on.

rav: Good. Drafting acceptance criteria. Drop comments.

leah: Also demand for per-route SLAs. Chat wants low-latency lanes; batch embedding can be cheaper.

rav: Draft acceptance criteria (comments inline):
- Availability: 99.9% for hosted routed paths (phase-1 target)
- Latency objectives: regional chat lane median <40ms, p95 <150ms; embeddings best-effort
- Affinity semantics: UI toggle with two modes: soft (best-effort) and strict (hard-pin)
- Billing: clear addon SKU for strict affinity and per-route QoS
- Telemetry: per-tenant per-route token/sec, route-failures, fallback counts, and topology-placements exposed to customer
- Rollout: canary across 1 dev org + 2 small named accounts, automated rollback triggers

tom: Add migration safety checks: KV cache warm-up window, expected cold-start penalty, and steady-state token distribution test.

jordana: For sales: require a template SLA addendum for strict affinity customers. Negotiate limit on guaranteed throughput unless they buy reserved capacity.

rav: Ops, what are reasonable automated rollback thresholds?

tom: Propose: error rate delta > 0.75% absolute OR p95 latency > 40% relative increase OR fallback rate spike > 1% sustained for 5min.

leah: Also require a data residency validation: verify region tag on storage and logs; legal needs a checklist.

rav: On ownership: suggest Platform owns the routing engine and policy DSL; Product owns defaults, pricing, and customer UX. Document this in RFC.

jordana: Who's building the pricing model? Product + Finance; we need a quick estimate of incremental infra cost for hard-pin per tenant.

tom: I'll run a simulation: sample 50 tenants with hard-pin and measure capacity delta; aim to deliver numbers by Wed.

leah: UX ask: admin page should show affected hosts/nodes, expected cost delta, and an undo button. Undo should trigger immediate de-provisioning when safe.

rav: That undo story is critical — customers want a revert with predictable latency. Add to gating criteria.

deploy-bot: RFC draft created: "segmentation-routing-roadmap-v2" https://r.wd/r/seg-v2. Feedback requested.

tom: Tests we need pre-GA: noisy-tenant flood, cross-region latency injection, KV chain stress, and model fallback correctness (ensure variant preserves semantics).

jordana: Also a comms pack: migration schedule, one-pager for named customers, and a standard postponement policy for customers in migration window.

rav: Launch gates I'm proposing:
- Safety: automated rollback works and has been exercised in staging
- Performance: p95/p99 within target across canary orgs for 48h
- Operability: runbook + SRE playbook for evictions and rollbacks
- Commercial: pricing SKUs and at least one signed pilot for strict affinity
- Compliance: data residency checklist sign-off for regions in scope

leah: Add acceptance test: swap routing policy mid-traffic and assert correctness on a set of golden prompts (quality metric).

tom: I'll own the noisy-tenant harness and the KV chain tests. Planning to use existing loadgen and extend it for region affinity.

jordana: I'll coordinate with Finance to model pricing buckets. Need Tom's infra delta numbers first.

rav: Ok next actions: Tom runs capacity sim by Wed, Jordana + Finance meet by Thu, Leah to mock admin UX by EOD tomorrow, I'll fold all into RFC and tag reviewers. Flag anything that must be in P1 now.

leah: One more — we should log assumptions clearly: e.g., expected average session lengths, burst patterns, and model sequence-length distribution. Helps infra sims.

rav: Good call. Add assumptions section to RFC. Thanks team.
